summary.text: Jim McGovern is the incumbent for Massachusetts's 2nd District and is unopposed on the November general-election ballot.

A Worcester native and former longtime aide to Rep. Joe Moakley, he was first elected in 1996 and is the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee, also serving on the Agriculture Committee and as co-chair of the House Hunger Caucus.
His official biography emphasizes his work on hunger and human rights.

paragraphs.text: McGovern was born in Worcester, Massachusetts, and raised in the city's Burncoat neighborhood, according to his official biography; his parents own a small package store and his sisters are public school teachers.

He studied at American University in Washington, D.C.; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree (1981) and a master's degree (1984), and his official biography says he earned a B.A. in history while working his way through college.

His official biography says he began as a volunteer on Sen. George McGovern's 1972 presidential campaign as a seventh grader and later sought an internship in the senator's office while at American University.
McGovern then worked for over a decade, 14 years according to Ballotpedia, as a senior aide to the late U.S. Rep. John Joseph Moakley (D) of South Boston.

In 1990 he led the Moakley Commission's congressional investigation into the 1989 murder of six Jesuit priests, their housekeeper, and her daughter in El Salvador by the Salvadoran Army, and the commission's report led to a change in U.S. foreign aid policy.
He ran for Congress in 1996, took office in 1997, and has been reelected every two years since.
McGovern has been the top Democrat on the House Rules Committee since 2018 and, according to his official biography, chaired it during the 116th and 117th Congresses.
He serves on the House Agriculture Committee, where his office says he worked to secure a White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health, and he is co-chair of the House Hunger Caucus.

He also serves on the Congressional-Executive Commission on China and the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, and his official biography lists legislation he authored that became law, including the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, the Tibet Policy and Support Act, and the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act.
According to the same biography, he is married to Lisa Murray McGovern and they have two children.
